content.title: How to watch the 2026 WNBA draft on ESPN - ESPN
content.text: ESPNApr 15, 2026, 08:15 PM ETReactionsAfter months of negotiations, culminating in a week of marathon bargaining sessions last month, the WNBA and the players' association verbally agreed to a new collective bargaining agreement March 18. That meant the league would have to conduct an expansion draft, free agency and the WNBA draft in a compressed offseason before the 30th season tips off May 8.So here we are, with players officially able to sign contracts beginning April 11.Check out the latest buzz, news and reports surrounding the WNBA.Jump to: Core designationsMore links: Trade grades | WNBA draft | Ranking the free agentsApril 15Free agent point guard Odyssey Sims has agreed to a one-year deal with the Dallas Wings, her agent told ESPN. Sims was the No. 2 pick from the 2014 WNBA draft, as well as a 2019 All-WNBA and All-Star selection.The New York Liberty have re-signed Betnijah Laney-Hamilton.A'ja Wilson is signing a three-year, $5 million contract to return to the Las Vegas Aces. The deal is fully guaranteed and is the largest in WNBA history.Chennedy Carter has signed a training camp contract with the Las Vegas Aces. The No. 4 pick in the 2020 WNBA draft, Carter last played in the league in 2024. The former WNBA All-Rookie selection has averaged 14.6 points, 2.5 rebounds and 2.8 assists over 84 career games.April 14Three-time WNBA champion Alysha Clark has agreed to a one-year deal with the Dallas Wings, her agent told ESPN. Clark was previously with the Washington Mystics.Free agent Temi Fagbenle has signed with the Toronto Tempo on a one-year deal worth $1 million, per her agent. Fagbenle was most recently with the Golden State Valkyries.Three-time Canadian Olympian Kia Nurse has signed a one-year deal with the Tempo. Nurse was previously with the Chicago Sky and becomes the first Canadian player to join the Tempo's inaugural roster.Monique Akoa Makani is signing a two-year deal to return to the Phoenix Mercury, a source told ESPN.April 13Restricted free agent Shakira Austin is returning to the Washington Mystics on a three-year deal worth $3.57 million, sources told ESPN. Austin had signed an offer sheet with the Toronto Tempo with those terms, but Washington matched them. Austin has played all three seasons of her WNBA career with the Mystics.Myisha Hines-Allen has signed with the Indiana Fever, the team announced. Hines-Allen spent last season with the Dallas Wings.Stephanie Talbot has signed a one-year deal with the Las Vegas Aces, ESPN's Alexa Philippou confirmed. Talbot was most recently with the New York Liberty.Brianna Turner has signed with the Las Vegas Aces, the team announced. Turner spent last season with the Indiana Fever.The details of Jewell Loyd's three-year, $2.2 million-plus deal with the Las Vegas Aces have been confirmed to ESPN's Andraya Carter. Loyd will be paid $800,000 in 2026, $840,000 in 2027 and $860,000 in 2028.Rebecca Allen and Pauline Astier have signed one-year deals with the New York Liberty, ESPN's Alexa Philippou confirmed. Allen had spent her first seven seasons in the league with the Liberty. Astier is a French point guard.The Las Vegas Aces have re-signed Dana Evans, ESPN's Kareem Copeland confirmed. Evans had joined the Aces last season after four years in Chicago.Kayla Thornton has signed a one-year deal with the Golden State Valkyries, ESPN's Kendra Andrews. Thornton sat out the second half of last season after suffering a season-ending knee injury in July.The Las Vegas Aces have re-signed NaLyssa Smith, ESPN's Kareem Copeland reported.April 12Emma Cannon signed a one-year vet minimum deal at $292,500 to return to the Los Angeles Sparks, her agent told ESPN's Alexa Philippou.Kahleah Copper, DeWanna Bonner and Sami Whitcomb have re-signed with the Phoenix Mercury, the team announced. Copper's deal is for two years, a source told ESPN's Kendra Andrews.Megan Gustafson is signing a two-year deal -- $500,000 in the first year and $525,000 in the second -- to join the Portland Fire, ESPN's Alexa Philippou reported. Gustafson spent the past two seasons with the Aces.Jade Melbourne is signing a one-year deal for $500,000 to return to the Seattle Storm, with whom she started her WNBA career in 2023, ESPN's Alexa Philippou reported. Melbourne spent the past two seasons in Washington with the Mystics.Czech duo Eliska Hamzova and Emma Cechova have signed with the Minnesota Lynx, sources confirmed to ESPN's Kareem Copeland.DiJonai Carrington is signing a one-year deal with the Chicago Sky, ESPN's Alexa Philippou reported. Carrington has had stints with the Connecticut Sun, Dallas Wings and, last season, Minnesota Lynx.Natasha Howard is signing with the Minnesota Lynx on a two-year, $1.4 million deal, sources told ESPN's Ramona Shelburne. Howard is returning to Minnesota, where she won a title in 2017. She has also had stints with the Seattle Storm, New York Liberty, Dallas Wings and Indiana Fever.Nia Coffey is signing a two-year deal above the veteran minimum with the Minnesota Lynx, ESPN's Kendra Andrews reported. Coffey most recently was in Atlanta for five seasons.The Golden State Valkyries have signed forward Laeticia Amihere, guard Kaitlyn Chen, Greek center Mariella Fasoula and Australian guard Miela Sowah to training camp contracts, the team announced.Kayla McBride is returning to the Minnesota Lynx on a two-year, lower max salary deal, ESPN's Ramona Shelburne reported. McBride has been with the Lynx since 2021.Ezi Magbegor has re-signed with the Seattle Storm, the team has announced. Magbegor has spent her entire career (since 2020) in Seattle.The Dallas Wings have signed Shyanne Sellers, Amy Okonkwo, Costanza Verona and Dulcy Fankam Mendjiadeu to training camp contracts, the team announced.The Golden State Valkyries have re-signed Iliana Rupert and Janelle Salaun to multiyear deals, and Cecilia Zandalasini to a one-year contract, the team announced.Kaila Charles is re-signing with the Golden State Valkyries on a two-year deal, sources told Andscape's Sean Hurd and ESPN's Kareem Copeland. Charles joined the expansion franchise last season.Courtney Vandersloot has re-signed with the Chicago Sky on a two-year deal worth $750,000 per year, the team announced. Vandersloot played just seven games last season before a season-ending ACL injury.Courtney Williams is returning to the Minnesota Lynx on a two-year max deal, sources told ESPN's Alexa Philippou. Williams' deal is for $2.4 million over the two years.The Chicago Sky and Los Angeles Sparks have agreed to a trade that will send Rickea Jackson to the Sky and Ariel Atkins to the Sparks, sources told ESPN's Alexa Philippou. Atkins will get a multiyear deal from the Sparks.MORE: Trade Grades: Sky get Jackson, Sparks get Atkins, one gets an AGabby Williams has agreed to a multiyear deal with the Golden State Valkyries, ESPN's Andraya Carter confirmed. Williams previously played for the Seattle Storm and Chicago Sky.Isabelle Harrison has signed a one-year deal with the Toronto Tempo, sources confirmed to ESPN's Andraya Carter. Harrison spent last season playing for the New York Liberty.Kelsey Plum is signing a $999,999 one-year deal to return to the Los Angeles Sparks, ESPN's Shams Charania reported. Plum had joined the Sparks last year after six seasons with the Las Vegas Aces -- and a season with the San Antonio Stars before that.Sophie Cunningham is returning to the Indiana Fever on a one-year deal, sources told ESPN's Alexa Philippou. Cunningham had joined the Fever last season after six seasons in Phoenix.April 11Alanna Smith has agreed to a three-year max contract with the Dallas Wings, her agent told ESPN's Alexa Philippou. Earned co-Defensive Player of the Year honors last year at Minnesota.Cheyenne Parker-Tyus is re-signing with the Las Vegas Aces on a one-year deal, ESPN's Alexa Philippou confirmed. Parker-Tyus appeared in only two regular-season games last season for the Aces.Stefanie Dolson is signing with the Seattle Storm, ESPN's Alexa Philippou confirmed. Most recently played for Washington last season, and has won WNBA titles with both Chicago and New York.Kennedy Burke is signing a one-year deal with the Connecticut Sun, sources told Alexa Philippou. She spent the past two seasons with New York.Tyasha Harris is signing with the Indiana Fever following stints in Dallas and Connecticut, sources confirmed to ESPN's Alexa Philippou.Bridget Carleton has officially signed a three-year deal at the max with the Portland Fire, ESPN's Alexa Philippou confirmed. Carleton was selected No. 1 overall by the Fire in the expansion draft.Veronica Burton has signed a multiyear deal to return to the Golden State Valkyries, the team announced.The Atlanta Dream have officially re-signed Rhyne Howard, the team announced.Erica Wheeler is returning to the Los Angeles Sparks, where she played in 2021, ESPN confirmed. She had spent last season with the Seattle Storm.Shakira Austin has signed a three-year offer sheet with the Toronto Tempo, sources told ESPN's Kareem Copeland. The Washington Mystics have two days to match the offer sheet for the restricted free agent.Jonquel Jones is re-signing with the New York Liberty on a multiyear deal, ESPN's Kendra Andrews confirmed.Skylar Diggins has signed with the Chicago Sky on a two-year deal, sources told ESPN's Alexa Philippou. The seven-time All-Star had spent the past two seasons with the Seattle Storm.Satou Sabally is signing a multiyear deal with the New York Liberty, ESPN reported. Sabally spent last season with the Phoenix Mercury.Monique Billings is signing with the Indiana Fever, ESPN's Alexa Philippou confirmed. Billings spent last season with the Golden State Valkyries.Dearica Hamby is returning to the Los Angeles Sparks on a three-year, fully guaranteed deal for close to $3.5 million, ESPN's Alexa Philippou reported.The Chicago Sky have acquired guard Jacy Sheldon from the Washington Mystics, ESPN's Alexa Philippou reported. In exchange, Washington receives Chicago's 2028 first-round pick.Restricted free agent Lexie Hull is returning to the Indiana Fever on a multiyear deal, ESPN's Alexa Philippou confirmed.The Toronto Tempo have signed Laura Juškaitė to a training camp contract, ESPN's Alexa Philippou reported. The Lithuanian recently won a EuroCup championship with Mersin.Azura Stevens is signing a three-year deal -- with a salary of $1 million in 2026 that increases 5% from that base each year thereafter -- to return to the Chicago Sky, ESPN's Alexa Philippou reported. She was with Chicago from 2020 to '22 before spending the past three seasons with the Los Angeles Sparks.April 10Two-time WNBA scoring champion Brittney Griner is finalizing a seven-figure deal to join the Connecticut Sun, sources confirmed to ESPN's Alexa Philippou on Friday. The team later announced the deal is for one year.Jordin Canada will stay with the Atlanta Dream, re-signing for two years at $1.2-plus million, ESPN's Kareem Copeland reported.Free agent star Chelsea Gray has reached a three-year, $3 million fully guaranteed deal to return to the Las Vegas Aces, a source told ESPN's Kendra Andrews on Friday.All-defensive center Elizabeth Williams has agreed to re-sign with the Chicago Sky for $1.2 million over two years, fully guaranteed, ESPN's Chiney Ogwumike reported.Jessica Shepard has agreed to a multiyear deal with the Dallas Wings, ESPN's Alexa Philippou reported. She had spent all five seasons of her career with the Minnesota Lynx, including playing a key role off the bench last year.Natisha Hiedeman has agreed to a two-year deal with the Seattle Storm, sources confirmed to ESPN's Alexa Philippou. She was a key player off the bench for the Minnesota Lynx.Kelsey Mitchell is finalizing a one-year agreement at the $1.4 million supermax to return to the Indiana Fever, ESPN's Chiney Ogwumike reported.Four-time WNBA All-Star Arike Ogunbowale is signing a seven-figure, multiyear deal to return to the Dallas Wings, sources told ESPN's Alexa Philippou on Friday. Ogunbowale was eligible for the $1.4 million supermax after being cored by the Wings, but she is taking less than that for the team to be able to build a quality roster around her, sources said.Naz Hillmon is finalizing a three-year deal to return to the Atlanta Dream, sources told ESPN's Kendra Andrews. Her contract is worth $2.5 million-plus over three years, fully guaranteed.Jewell Loyd is sticking with the Las Vegas Aces and finalizing a three-year deal with the team, a source told ESPN's Andraya Carter on Friday. ESPN's Kareem Copeland confirmed the deal is for three years and $2.2-plus million.Allisha Gray is finalizing a three-year max-plus deal with the Atlanta Dream, a source told Andscape's Sean Hurd. The terms will be $3.7 million over three years, per Hurd.Four-time All-Star Brionna Jones is finalizing a multiyear deal to return to the Atlanta Dream, a source told Andscape's Sean Hurd.Perennial MVP contender Alyssa Thomas is finalizing a deal to return to the Phoenix Mercury, a source told Andscape's Sean Hurd.Guards Marina Mabrey and Brittney Sykes have agreed to terms to join the Toronto Tempo, their agent Marcus Crenshaw of The FAM Sports Agency told ESPN's Alexa Philippou on Friday. With each agreeing to two-year deals at about the max in Year 1, they are the first known million-dollar backcourt pairing under the WNBA's new collective bargaining agreement. Mabrey's contract is for two years, $2.4 million total ($1.2M in 2026 and $1.2M in 2027).Nneka Ogwumike intends to return to the Los Angeles Sparks, her sister, ESPN analyst Chiney Ogwumike, posted on social media on Friday. Nneka Ogwumike previously played 12 seasons in Los Angeles, where she won the MVP in 2016, the same year she led the Sparks to their third WNBA championship. April 9Nneka Ogwumike, who has played the past two seasons with Seattle, announced in a social media post that she will not be returning to the Storm. Ogwumike is a former MVP and 10-time All-Star. The Las Vegas Aces are finalizing an agreement for Jackie Young to return, sources told ESPN's Alexa Philippou. The deal is expected to be a one-year contract at the regular max ($1.19 million).The Dallas Wings have traded forward Diamond Miller to the Connecticut Sun in exchange for center/forward Rayah Marshall.April 8Satou Sabally will not return to the Phoenix Mercury. "My best year yet. Thank you Phoenix," Sabally wrote in an Instagram post. Sabally helped lead the Mercury to the 2025 WNBA Finals. April 7Ten of 15 WNBA teams have extended core qualifying offers to players since free agency started Monday:• Atlanta Dream: Allisha Gray • Chicago Sky: Ariel Atkins • Dallas Wings: Arike Ogunbowale • Indiana Fever: Kelsey Mitchell • Los Angeles Sparks: Kelsey Plum • Minnesota Lynx: Napheesa Collier • New York Liberty: Sabrina Ionescu • Portland Fire: Bridget Carleton • Seattle Storm: Ezi Magbegor • Toronto Tempo: Marina MabreyThe WNBA's core player designation is akin to the NFL franchise tag. A team can "core" a player to prevent them from becoming an unrestricted free agent by retaining their exclusive rights.The core designation gives a team exclusive negotiating rights to a player and comes with a baseline contract of a fully guaranteed one-year deal worth the supermax ($1.4 million in 2026), though the player can negotiate different terms.The core designation can also be a way for a team to prevent a player from walking in free agency without getting anything in return as it ultimately executes a sign-and-trade with the star. -- Alexa PhilippouApril 6The Chicago Sky traded two-time WNBA All-Star Angel Reese to the Atlanta Dream for first-round draft picks in 2027 and '28, ESPN's Kendra Andrews reported. The Dream also received 2028 second-round swap rights.MORE: Trade grades: Dream get Reese, Sky get picks, one gets an AApril 3A'ja Wilson, a four-time MVP and three-time WNBA champion, said she has no intentions of leaving the Las Vegas Aces when free agency opens.April 1Breanna Stewart will be re-signing with the New York Liberty in free agency, the two-time WNBA MVP and three-time league champion announced on her podcast.Additionally, Liberty teammate Sabrina Ionescu, the Liberty's No. 1 overall draft pick in 2020, told reporters at USA Basketball training camp that she also intends to return to New York.
